verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure—the verifier's FAIL is correct. The GSO harness compared the agent patch against baseline and reference commit 061c2e9190 ("PERF: merge on monotonic keys"), reporting opt_commit=False, continuous reward 0.867, and binary_reward 0 because reward did not exceed the 1.20 pass threshold [1][2][3]. The task asked for general merge_ordered speedups while preserving correctness and pursuing the best possible speedup [4], but the agent's final change is only a narrow monotonic fast-path in get_join_indexers that calls libjoin.*_join_indexer after ndarray monotonicity checks and only when at least one key side is unique [5]. That direction suffices for the instruction benchmark—the agent measured 0.2577s before patching [6] and celebrated ~0.0039s afterward [7]—and the hidden verifier confirms test 0 dropping from ~0.29s to ~0.004s, matching the reference commit on that workload [8]. However, on broader held-out scenarios the patch stalls far short of the reference: test 14 (multi-merge workload with NaN-laced, duplicate float keys) stays ~0.75s versus ~0.77s baseline while the reference commit runs ~0.46s, and test 15 shows the same pattern (~0.65s patch vs ~0.43s commit) [9][10], yielding the sub-threshold gm_speedup_patch_commit score. The agent never saw these tests and relied on its own benchmark plus pandas merge unit tests, which was insufficient to catch the large generalization gap [6][7]. The reference commit is a broader merge refactor beyond the agent's single fast-path block, and the verifier benchmarks against that full commit [3]. Outcome is TN: verifier correctly failed a partial optimization that does not truly meet the task's performance bar.
